excerpt: You pay your debts on time, every household has electricity, and most of your young people finish lower secondary school.
paras: You pay your debts on time, every household has electricity, and most of your young people finish lower secondary school. Yet you finance yourself almost entirely at home, at the cost of your own companies. Let your institutions and your sun open cheaper capital from abroad.

Your partners are investing in your water and your power. In March 2026 the World Bank approved $208.5 million for drinking water and $124 million for irrigation, after $430 million in 2025 for a more reliable and efficient grid. In July 2026 the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development approved €50 million for solar power and battery storage at Tataouine.

The work ahead is plain, and it is worth saying plainly. At the last count, in 2011, sixty-five in every hundred of your children reached the end of primary school unable to read a simple text. Only sixty-five in every hundred of you have safely managed drinking water. Twenty-four in every hundred of you cannot always count on enough good food. Reading sets your Coverage today, at 34.5 out of 100, with water and food close behind. Each of them is within your reach.

Now imagine that same resolve turned toward every home in the country. Picture Perfect Tunisia: a morning when every family cooks with clean fuel and sits down to a full table; when every tap runs clean and every home has a safe toilet; when every child walks to a school where a teacher is waiting, and reads with ease by the age of ten; when every mother lives within reach of a clinic with the lights on, and every young person finds work that pays. And no Tunisian falls below a decent life, because the nation has decided that none will.
quote: A nation that pays on time should borrow at the price of its word.
